items.independentDerivation: Differentiation gives P'(x)=4x^3-18x^2+22x-4 and P''(x)=12x^2-36x+22. At 2, these give P(2)=0, P'(2)=0 and P''(2)=-2, proving exact multiplicity two. The remaining roots have sum 6-4=2 and product -4/4=-1, hence satisfy x^2-2x-1=0. Its discriminant is 8, giving 1±sqrt(2). Both are real, distinct and different from 2. Independently multiplying (x^2-4x+4)(x^2-2x-1) gives exactly the supplied quartic.

items.independentDerivation: P'(x)=4x^3-3x^2-26x-8 and P''(x)=12x^2-6x-26. Substitution gives P(-2)=0, P'(-2)=0 and P''(-2)=34, so -2 is exactly double. The remaining roots have sum 1-(-4)=5 and product 12/4=3. Thus x^2-5x+3=0 has discriminant 13 and roots (5±sqrt(13))/2. They are real and distinct; substituting -2 into this quadratic gives 17, excluding overlap. Multiplying (x^2+4x+4)(x^2-5x+3) reproduces every supplied coefficient.

items.independentDerivation: P'(x)=3(x^2+2x-8). Product -8 and sum 2 select 4 and -2, giving derivative zeroes -4 and 2. P(2)=k-28 and P(-4)=k+80, so the exhaustive possibilities are k=28 and k=-80. P''(x)=6x+6 gives 18 and -18 respectively, proving both roots are exactly double. Root sum -3 gives the remaining roots -7 and 5. Expansion yields (x-2)^2(x+7)=x^3+3x^2-24x+28 and (x+4)^2(x-5)=x^3+3x^2-24x-80.

items.independentDerivation: Evenness gives P(-3)=P(3)=0; oddness of P' gives P'(-3)=-P'(3)=0; evenness of P'' transfers its nonzero value at the given exact double root. Thus -3 is exactly double too. The two distinct double roots exhaust the monic quartic, giving (x-3)^2(x+3)^2=(x^2-9)^2=x^4-18x^2+81. Therefore p=-18 and q=81. Independently, P'(3)=108+6p=0 gives p=-18, P(3)=81+9p+q=0 gives q=81, and P''(±3)=72 confirms exact multiplicities.

items.independentDerivation: For a triple root r, P''(r)=6Ar+2B=0. Since A≠0, r=-B/(3A). Then P'(r)=3Ar^2+2Br+C=B^2/(3A)-2B^2/(3A)+C=C-B^2/(3A)=0, proving B^2=3AC. No division by B or C occurs, so B=0 is included and forces r=C=0; the assumed triple root then also forces D=0. P'''=6A≠0 ensures exact multiplicity three. The stated implication is necessary, and the answer does not incorrectly claim sufficiency.

items.independentDerivation: Parity gives P(-beta)=0, P'(-beta)=0 and P''(-beta)=P''(beta)≠0, proving the opposite root is exactly double. Since beta≠0, the roots are distinct and exhaust degree four. Monicity gives P(x)=(x-beta)^2(x+beta)^2=x^4-2beta^2x^2+beta^4, so a=-2beta^2 and b=beta^4. Explicit real nonzero beta ensures beta^2>0 and beta^4>0, proving both strict signs. Independently, P'(beta)=2beta(2beta^2+a)=0 yields the same a, then P(beta)=0 gives b; P''(±beta)=8beta^2>0 confirms exact multiplicities.
